observed: Execution source, real Procgen CPU smoke and the single live GPU PID are verified.
The zero-step 128-episode stochastic full-distribution baseline completed at mean return 3.125 and success rate 31.25%.
Training completed exactly 25,165,824 transitions / 1,536 PPO updates without NaN, OOM or process failure.
The final periodic 128-episode evaluation reached mean return 8.828125 and success rate 88.28125%.
The independent final 512-episode evaluation reached mean return 8.671875 and success rate 86.71875%, passing both preregistered thresholds.
interpretation: The combined public-recipe alignment explains a substantial part of CR-PPO-0001 underperformance under the tested seed and runtime.

This establishes that the old result was not merely a deterministic/fixed-level evaluation artifact, because the old checkpoint had already remained at 4.9609375 under the same 512-episode stochastic full-distribution metric.
not_established: Which individual recipe difference is causally responsible; this run changed a package of training and evaluation settings.
That every deviation from the public recipe is a software bug rather than an alternative but weaker configuration.
A strict paper reproduction across framework, Procgen version and multiple seeds.
Authorization to collect replacement trajectories or start dynamics.
decision: Treat the aligned recipe as the validated default for future from-scratch PPO runs.
Add a machine-enforced final-policy quality gate before any trajectory collection.
Run separately preregistered single-variable controls before assigning the old performance gap to one training bug.
Do not start dynamics or collect replacement trajectories under CR-PPO-0002.
